_readme: THIS FILE IS JAMES'S JUDGEMENT. tools/build-registry-graph.mjs merges it with live
`gh repo list` facts and REFUSES to label any repo that is not named here.
Why it exists: the generator used to sort the registry by pushedAt and label the top
14. With 24 public active repos that named 58% of them, which is a listing, not a
curation — a bubble-pop game rendered at the same weight as a package with 95 stars.
Push recency is a fact about a README typo, not about value.
- A repo here that no longer exists on GitHub aborts the build. No silent drop.
- A PRIVATE repo is only labelled when its entry carries `disclosed`, naming where
it is already public. Private repos never get a `code` link.
- `proves` may contain {stars} and {forks}. They are substituted from the live gh
call at build time, so a number on the page can never go stale against its source.
- `what` is one sentence a non-engineer can read. `proves` is the evidence a
sceptic would ask for. If an entry has no honest `proves`, it is not flagship.
TIERS decide node radius. Radius used to be disk usage, which made a repo full of
video assets the biggest thing on screen.

core.disclosed: named in prose in the section lede on this page
core.what: The autonomous agent that manages the rest of the registry — it reads the repos, opens the work, and reports to Discord without being asked.
core.proves: 97 modules, 60,795 lines of first-party code, running unattended on a Mac Mini.

entries.what: The first MCP server for Final Cut Pro XML — drive a professional video timeline with natural language.
entries.proves: {stars} stars and {forks} forks from developers who found it on their own. 11 releases published to PyPI.

entries.disclosed: named in the CLEARED GATES section on this page
entries.what: Sports-betting analytics platform built for a paying client and running in production.
entries.proves: Live at betmetrics.ca with real users and a paid engagement behind it.

entries.what: Generates an artist website as a named world rather than a template — it derives type, colour and motion from the artist's own premise.
entries.proves: Two blind judges could not pick the generated site out of a lineup. It refuses to print a number it cannot source.

entries.what: This site, plus a full draggable desktop OS at /os — 20 apps and 46 vanilla modules with no framework and no runtime dependencies.
entries.proves: Zero runtime dependencies. Every number on this page traces to a generator that exits non-zero rather than invent one.

entries.disclosed: linked as OPEN THE LIVE DASHBOARD on this page
entries.what: Mission control for the agent — the surface that shows what it ran, what it changed, and what it is blocked on.
entries.proves: Serving live agent telemetry daily. The public view runs on demo data so client names never leave the machine.

entries.what: The music-video directing catalogue — the other half of the career, kept deliberately separate from the engineering surface.
entries.proves: Live, and the source of record for the directing credits claimed on this page.

entries.what: Content-creator and Twitch-streamer site built for a client, shipped end to end.
entries.proves: Deployed and handed over, with contact delivery verified by receipt rather than by the page's success banner.

entries.what: Desktop app that generates character sprite sheets — 8 directions and 100+ actions from one text prompt.
entries.proves: A native desktop binary, not a web demo. Written in Go with a React front end.

entries.what: macOS anti-infostealer toolkit that blocks curl-pipe-shell paste attacks and audits how far a leaked secret would reach.
entries.proves: Written after a real ClickFix attack, not from a threat report. Defensive use only.

entries.what: Six browser games that teach generative-AI concepts by playing them — prompt craft, hallucination hunting, red teaming.
entries.proves: Spaced repetition on the FSRS algorithm, so retention is scheduled rather than hoped for.

entries.what: Structured prompt builder for image and video models — Veo, Sora, Kling, Nano Banana.
entries.proves: {stars} stars and {forks} forks, and it runs on its own domain.

entries.what: Retrieval-augmented generation that will not answer without citing the passage it used.
entries.proves: Built to make an unsourced answer structurally impossible rather than discouraged.
